answer: Each identity monthly types a dictation — a whisper of tide tables and a walnut inventory — live for 12 minutes while verifiers record keystroke dwell, flight time and correction rhythm, hash-posted at enrolment. Pairwise tests compare distributions: scripts cluster near-identically and one operator cannot hold two stable cadences, so a match above 0.92 merges slots and refuses entry. Scaling to 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 typists at $25 monthly ($25,000) plus 200 hours, with no automation shortcut. Trade-off: injury or a new keyboard shifts cadence, so honest agents need supervised re-enrolment.
